document.title: Trusted Implementation Lifecycle — Technical Design
document.summary: An always-on parent extension handles an idle direct human mutation request before the primary agent, creating a durable fail-closed transaction with one path-confined writer, immutable verification/review evidence, bounded repair, and human integration.
document.reviewFocus: Confirm the input/write interception seam, candidate and receipt ownership, child-role capability boundaries, headless verification, repair invalidation, and fail-closed behavior.
sources: Pi extension documentation: input, before_agent_start, tool_call, agent_settled
Product owner architecture approval: automatic local lifecycle and Alphonse ChangeExecutor adapters, 2026-09-01

sections.title: Automatic implementation must become controller-owned before mutation
sections.summary: The approved PRD requires normal conversational entry, deterministic mutation interception, independent evidence, bounded repair, and human integration without a command or skill gate.

items: Authority
Approved PRD: docs/features/trusted-implementation-lifecycle/prd.document.json
Acceptance
scenario-001 through scenario-004 and ac-001 through ac-004
Current seams
Pi input/tool_call lifecycle, agent-jobs detached launcher, verify runner, and Git worktree helpers
Boundary
Trusted local Git repositories first; real process containment remains required before untrusted unattended execution

blocks.decision: Make one always-loaded ImplementationLifecycleController the mutation admission and delivery-completion authority for direct Pi sessions.
blocks.recommendation: In input, accept only an idle direct interactive TUI user request with explicit edit/implementation intent, atomically create the root lease, return handled, and start the transaction before any primary agent runs. For all other turns, a deny-by-default tool_call barrier permits audited read-only tools only, blocks unauthorized mutations without creating authority, marks the whole batch blocked, and aborts the primary run. Capture a complete clean-or-dirty Git snapshot, launch path-confined child roles, verify a disposable candidate snapshot, persist the immutable evidence tuple, and return a human integration decision.
blocks.goal: Implementation requested through normal Pi conversation cannot mutate or complete outside a candidate-bound verifier and independent review lifecycle.
blocks.shape: ImplementationLifecycleController owns admission and policy; DeliveryRunStore alone owns the atomic cross-process root lease and durable evidence; CandidateWorkspace captures complete nonignored base/candidate trees and disposable verification snapshots; HeadlessPiRoleRunner launches no-discovery children with one controller-owned path guard extension; ExplicitVerifier owns executable gates; the primary session owns user communication only.
blocks.why: The input boundary is the only point that can bind trusted direct-human authority before an agent turn; tool_call is the final effect boundary for every other turn. Parent orchestration plus controller-owned role profiles prevents the writer or candidate from changing policy, verification, reviewer authority, receipts, or integration state.
blocks.approve: Add interactive-only admission, provenance/effect-bound read-only primary tools, atomic root lease, complete snapshot, one guarded no-shell writer, protected verification closure, controller-profiled read-only reviewer, two pre-counted repairs, process-stopped cancellation/reload reattachment, durable fail-closed records, and zero-integration terminal outcomes.
blocks.notBuilding: A /deliver command, skill-triggered enforcement, mutable worker fan-out, automatic merge, unbounded retries, project-local controller policy, or a shared Alphonse runtime package.
blocks.risks: Child Pi processes retain host identity and provider credentials unless separately contained. Version one therefore omits writer bash/PowerShell and confines built-in edits through a controller-owned guard extension, but this remains trusted-local rather than an OS sandbox. Intent classification is authority-sensitive and must fail closed on ambiguity.
blocks.readiness: Approved by the product owner on 2026-09-01; implementation must fail closed when repository, verifier, candidate, or child-role proof is unavailable.

sections.title: The primary session cannot be both an unrestricted writer and its own delivery controller
sections.summary: Current extensions provide useful pieces, but none owns the complete authority-to-candidate lifecycle or prevents a normal agent from writing before those pieces run.

items: agent-jobs can persist detached processes but marks model/process termination rather than accepted software quality.
verify runs after interactive agent completion and intentionally skips headless contexts; it is not an explicit candidate-bound service.
worktree-manager creates feature branches from a configured base and may copy local hidden environment by default; delivery needs a current-base detached candidate with no environment copy.
before_agent_start can influence prompts but cannot enforce behavior; tool_call can block the actual edit/write/bash operation.
A child Pi process discovers the same global extensions unless launched with a restricted profile, creating controller recursion and capability leakage.
A session entry is conversational and ephemeral; restart-safe run state must live outside the transcript.

blocks.title: Rejected obvious seams
blocks.text: Do not rely on implement-task to remember the lifecycle, run verification only in agent_end, let the primary session mutate and review its own tree, or load the delivery extension inside writer/reviewer children. Each choice leaves self-certification or recursive authority in place.

sections.title: ImplementationLifecycleController owns mutation admission and terminal truth
sections.summary: Existing extensions become collaborators behind one controller instead of independent advisory features.

items.title: ImplementationLifecycleController
items.text: The input handler accepts only idle direct interactive TUI user input with explicit mutation intent, asks for clarification on ambiguity, atomically acquires the canonical-root lease, returns handled, and starts one run before the primary agent. before_agent_start selects controller-owned path-confined controller-owned read/grep/find/ls wrappers plus explicitly fingerprinted read-only tools; tool_call rejects any definition/provenance/input mismatch, blocks the remaining parallel batch, and calls ctx.abort(). Direct interactive ‘cancel implementation’ kills and waits for the child process group; session_before_switch refuses new/resume/fork until terminal, and reload adopts only a proven-dead lease, reconciles child evidence, and terminates non-favorably; it never resumes to the lease.

items.title: DeliveryRunStore
items.text: Is the sole manifest and receipt writer. It atomically acquires one cross-process lease per canonical Git common root, persists one atomically updated per-run manifest with append-only attempt evidence under the Git common directory at pi-delivery/runs; its terminal evidence becomes immutable and guards the active lease with nonce, PID, and process-start identity, and records trusted interactive request ID, authority digest, complete snapshots, exact primary/writer/reviewer tool/rubric/resource-profile digests, protected verification closure/results, supplied-review-input digest, repairCount, child process-group/exit evidence, cancellation, and terminal reason. It rejects stale or mismatched receipts.

items.title: CandidateWorkspace
items.text: Uses an alternate private Git index to capture the complete current nonignored clean-or-dirty working state—including staged, unstaged, untracked files, modes, symlinks, deletions, and renames—as a base tree without changing the user index. It creates one detached no-copy sibling worktree from that tree with hooks and fsmonitor disabled, freezes candidate trees, creates a disposable verification worktree from each candidate tree, and removes only manifest-owned paths.

items.title: HeadlessPiRoleRunner
items.text: Uses a controller-local stopped-start process-group primitive with durable pending-launch intent plus pre-release PID/start persistence, complete output hashing, TERM→KILL, and group-absence proof; agent-jobs remains independent. Each child disables discovered extensions, skills, prompt templates, and context files, then loads one explicit controller-owned role-policy extension and a controller-injected hashed role rubric. Writer/repair receives path-confined read/ls/edit/write only—no bash/PowerShell—and cannot reach Git/run-record paths. Reviewer receives path-confined read/ls plus a bounded report tool; candidate instructions are data only. Parent wrappers, never children, write authoritative logs and receipts.

items.title: ExplicitVerifier
items.text: Exports explicit verification as passed | failed | missing | timeout | mutated. It freezes and hashes the base verify script, package scripts/lockfile, CI/test/build configuration, and existing test suite as a protected closure; authorized exceptions are part of authority. It rejects candidate changes to that closure and exports the candidate into a standalone disposable snapshot without shared Git metadata, runs the frozen base gate and rejects added or changed tests whose execution cannot be proven, records command/result/output digest, recomputes the tree to detect side effects, and rejects missing, changed, weakened, timed-out, or mutating verification.

sections.title: One run manifest binds authority, candidate, verification, and review
sections.summary: The implementation is a small controller plus reusable services; existing feature commands and automatic verify behavior remain compatible.

blocks.label: Reference run contracts
Mutation admission decision
blocks.content:
on input:
  if active lease and direct interactive text means cancel: persist cancelling; TERM process group; wait; KILL after timeout; terminal only after parent-observed process-group exit evidence
  reject RPC/extension/queued/steering/follow-up authority
  if mode is rpc/json/print and request implies mutation: handle with fail-closed result
  if TUI is idle and direct interactive request explicitly authorizes mutation:
    canonicalize Git root; atomically acquire lease; persist AuthorityIdentity; return handled; acknowledge run ID; start controller
  if ambiguous mutation intent: return handled and ask one clarification
  otherwise select controller-owned controller-owned read/grep/find/ls wrappers plus provenance/effect-fingerprinted read-only tools

on primary tool_call without an authorized handled run:
  require tool object/provenance digest and input policy to match selected profile
  any mismatch or effect-capable/unknown tool: block, mark batch blocked, call ctx.abort(); create no authority

session_before_switch refuses new/resume/fork until terminal; reload/session_start adopts a lease only after matching PID/start identity proves the owner dead, fences the old nonce, stops the recorded group, and terminates non-favorably. Controller-issued children disable context/skills/prompts/discovered extensions and carry signed run/role provenance; writer omits bash/PowerShell. No prompt, workflow mode, sibling, or child can override policy.

blocks.label: Two-key completion and repair
blocks.content:
writer exits → freeze complete candidate tree; parent records child exit
reject final-candidate changes to the frozen base verify/package/CI/test-config/existing-test closure; export a standalone disposable candidate snapshot; run the frozen base gate; reject added/changed tests until an adapter can prove their execution; require unchanged verified tree
  eligible verifier failure = nonzero frozen command + unchanged policy/environment + candidate-specific signature
review exact tuple in fresh no-context/no-skills/no-prompts/no-discovered-extensions path-confined child using controller-injected rubric
  eligible review failure = validated Must/Should + candidate evidence + no protected-authority need
for eligible new signature while repairCount < 2: DeliveryRunStore invalidates receipts and increments repairCount before one fresh writer launch
missing/timeout/side-effect/provider/infrastructure/malformed/repeated/protected failure → FAILED SAFELY or DECISION REQUIRED; no repair
before merge-ready: audit no integration invocation; recheck primary snapshot, candidate tree, policy/results, reviewer profile, and supplied-input digest
matching pass + Proud + no Must/Should + complete writer/verifier/reviewer exit evidence → RunStore validates and hashes one canonical tuple through markMergeReady
controller and role command allowlists never advance a branch/ref, merge, push, remotely mutate, or deploy; Git may create one unreachable synthetic commit object solely as a detached-worktree anchor; primary files and integration state remain unchanged

sections.title: A blocked primary mutation becomes one detached candidate transaction
sections.summary: The path keeps authority in the original session and mutation in a child workspace while every acceptance signal binds to one candidate identity.

items.title: Capture authority
items.text: While Pi is idle, input accepts only a direct interactive TUI request with explicit mutation intent, canonicalizes the Git root, atomically acquires its cross-process lease, persists trusted request ID/source/digest, returns handled, and immediately acknowledges the run. Ambiguity asks once; print/JSON fails closed.

items.title: Intercept mutation
items.text: For every non-authorizing primary turn, the controller selects its own path-confined read wrappers plus tools whose exact definition/provenance/effect fingerprint and inputs are audited read-only. Any override, mismatch, edit/write/bash/PowerShell/custom/command/unknown effect is blocked without a run; the extension marks the parallel batch blocked and calls ctx.abort.

items.title: Prepare candidate
items.text: CandidateWorkspace uses a private alternate index to capture the complete current clean-or-dirty nonignored state as a tree, records modes/symlinks/deletes/renames through Git identity, creates a detached no-copy sibling worktree with hooks/fsmonitor disabled, and stores manifest ownership before effects.

items.title: Run writer
items.text: A headless Pi child disables discovered extensions and loads only the controller-owned role guard. The writer receives read/search/edit/write without bash/PowerShell; every path is confined to the candidate and Git/run records are denied. Parent process evidence—not child output—advances state.

items.title: Verify and review
items.text: ExplicitVerifier rejects changes or additions to the frozen base verify/package/CI/test-config/existing-test closure, exports a standalone disposable candidate snapshot without shared Git metadata, runs the frozen base gate, and rejects missing/timeout/policy weakening or any resulting nonignored tree change. Only a pass starts a no-context/no-skills/no-prompts/no-discovered-extensions path-confined reviewer with a controller-injected rubric and exact profile/input digest.

items.title: Repair or stop
items.text: Eligibility is positive: a nonzero frozen command under unchanged policy/environment, or a validated candidate-evidenced Must/Should finding requiring no protected authority. For a new signature while repairCount is below two, DeliveryRunStore invalidates receipts and increments repairCount before launch. Every other failure stops.

items.title: Publish terminal state
items.text: Immediately before terminalization, the controller audits zero integration invocation and rechecks the complete primary base, candidate tree, verification tuple, reviewer profile, and supplied-input digest. DeliveryRunStore persists one terminal state before one follow-up. Direct interactive Cancel waits for process-group exit; session switches refuse while nonterminal; reload adopts only a proven-dead lease, reconciles child evidence, and terminates non-favorably; it never resumes to the lease and reconciles child evidence.

sections.title: Three vertical outcomes establish automatic trusted delivery
sections.summary: Admission, evidence, and recovery are independently testable but compose through one run contract.

sections.title: Every approved requirement has one owning path and proof
sections.summary: The architecture keeps conversational activation, independent completion, and bounded human authority distinct.

blocks.title: Implementation activates without a special invocation
blocks.entryPoint: Idle direct interactive TUI input; deny-by-default tool_call only for unauthorized effects
blocks.contractState: Trusted idle direct input atomically owns one canonical-root lease and is handled before an agent turn; tool_call cannot create authority and denies every unaudited effect. One root may own only one cross-process run.
blocks.effect: A direct mutation request starts without a command, while unauthorized model mutation is blocked and aborts without a run.
blocks.failureRecovery: Ambiguous/untrusted input, print/JSON, repository failure, or lease collision fails safely before mutation; reload reconciles the existing run rather than duplicating it.
blocks.proof: ac-101 input provenance/mode, atomic lease, mixed-batch interception, complete dirty snapshot, and no-primary-mutation evidence.

blocks.title: The writer cannot certify itself
blocks.source: req-002; scenario-003 and scenario-004; ac-002 and ac-003
blocks.contractState: Writer is path-confined without shell/context/skills/prompts/discovered extensions and has no authoritative log/receipt capability; parent verification overlays the protected base closure, and controller-profiled read-only review binds one authority/base/complete-candidate/policy-result/reviewer-profile/supplied-input tuple; terminal policy requires both after final recheck.
blocks.effect: Only an unchanged tuple with passing disposable verification and Proud/no-Must-or-Should review produces merge-ready.
blocks.failureRecovery: Missing, timeout, mutating, malformed, failed, policy-weakened, or stale evidence advances only to eligible repair or safe termination and cannot be overridden by prose.
blocks.proof: ac-102 child path/ref escape, parent process evidence, complete snapshot, disposable verifier, review-input digest, and false-completion evidence.

blocks.title: Autonomous repair remains bounded by human authority
blocks.entryPoint: Concrete failed verifier/reviewer receipt or process restart
blocks.contractState: DeliveryRunStore invalidates receipts and increments repairCount before at most two fresh writers, only for the positive candidate-specific eligibility predicate; repeated/non-candidate/protected/ambiguous failure terminates; cancellation waits for child exit; audited terminal evidence never invokes integration.
blocks.effect: The run converges within authority or reports a precise human decision without hidden continuation or speculative restart resumption.
blocks.failureRecovery: Corrupt state, unresolved child, exhausted budget, authority conflict, or cleanup uncertainty stops and preserves candidate/evidence for inspection.
blocks.proof: ac-103 eligibility/count, process reconciliation, follow-up, immutable integration surfaces, and cleanup evidence.

sections.title: The parent process owns the transaction; role processes own bounded work
sections.summary: The diagram shows the only mutable role, deterministic evidence path, persistent state, and bounded repair feedback.

blocks.question: How does the parent Pi process admit a direct human mutation request before an agent turn and produce a restart-safe independently verified candidate?
blocks.caption: The always-on extension owns admission and state; child Pi roles operate with narrower capabilities in one candidate; verifier and reviewer receipts converge before human integration.
walkthrough: An idle direct interactive TUI mutation request is handled before a primary agent turn; unauthorized tool effects are denied without creating authority.

ImplementationLifecycleController atomically acquires the canonical-root lease and DeliveryRunStore records authority before CandidateWorkspace captures the complete clean/dirty base and creates the candidate.
A headless no-discovery writer with one explicit path guard is the only mutable role; it has no shell or receipt-writing authority.

ExplicitVerifier overlays the protected base verification/test closure on a disposable immutable candidate snapshot; only its passing tuple reaches a no-context/no-skill path-confined reviewer using a controller-owned hashed rubric/profile.

Positive eligible verifier/reviewer failures consume repairCount before at most two fresh repairs; direct Cancel waits for process-group exit, session switch refuses nonterminal state, and reload adopts only a proven-dead lease, reconciles child evidence, and terminates non-favorably; it never resumes to the lease.
A final recheck of authority, base, candidate, policy/results, and review input produces one terminal record and follow-up; every integration surface remains human-owned and unchanged.

sections.title: Trusted direct input owns activation; the write barrier enforces no unauthorized effects
sections.summary: This choice is blocking because another seam would make the lifecycle optional or permit mutation before evidence ownership exists.

blocks.question: Which boundary should activate and enforce direct Pi implementation delivery?
decisionDrivers: No user command, skill invocation, or workflow mode
Deterministic enforcement despite model routing errors
consequences: Idle direct interactive TUI input with explicit mutation intent creates authority, acquires the root lease, and is handled before a primary agent turn.
tool_call is deny-by-default for non-authorizing turns, creates no authority, blocks mixed mutation batches, and aborts the primary run.
Child roles disable discovered extensions and load one explicit controller guard; writer omits bash/PowerShell and is path-confined.
Worktree/tool policy remains trusted-local process safety rather than an OS sandbox claim.
blocks.revisitTrigger: Revisit if Pi gains a native first-class implementation transaction event or all mutable tools can be routed into an OS sandbox without a parent write barrier.

options.label: Always-on trusted-input admission plus deterministic effect barrier
options.summary: Handle an idle direct mutation request into a root lease before the agent; deny every unauthorized model-reachable effect without creating authority.
benefits: Cannot be skipped by model routing
costs: Requires explicit trusted-input classification and cross-process lease
Requires an audited read-only primary tool allowlist and child path guard
Ambiguous requests must ask rather than infer

options.label: Explicit command or implementation skill
options.summary: Ask the user or model to opt into the delivery workflow.
options.rejectionReason: Rejected explicitly by the product owner on 2026-09-01.

options.label: Let the primary write, then verify and review at agent end
options.summary: Retain the current mutable session and add post-hoc evidence.
options.rejectionReason: Rejected because the approved behavior requires isolated mutation and controller-owned completion.

blocks.rationale: Pi input can handle a direct human request before an agent turn, which is the only safe authority-creation seam. tool_call remains the final deterministic effect boundary for all other turns, ensuring no unauthorized model mutation occurs while never manufacturing permission from an attempted edit.

sections.title: Trust comes from negative tests and candidate identity, not agent narration
sections.summary: The verification strategy attacks bypass, false completion, stale evidence, repair drift, and unsafe recovery directly.

items: Input fixtures cover source, streaming behavior, idle state, explicit/ambiguous/non-mutation language, interactive TUI authority plus RPC/print/JSON failure.

Extension harness proves unauthorized write/edit/bash/PowerShell/custom/command and mixed parallel batches create no run, never execute, and abort; concurrent sessions race for one atomic canonical-root lease.
Temporary repositories prove alternate-index complete clean/dirty snapshots, modes/symlinks/deletes/renames, detached no-copy candidate, final base drift, and manifest-owned cleanup.

Child role-policy tests prove absolute/parent/symlink/Git-ref/run-record escapes are blocked, writer has no shell/context/skills/prompts/discovered extensions, reviewer uses a controller-hashed profile and treats candidate instructions as data, and only parent wrappers write process evidence/receipts.
Verifier fixtures prove frozen policy/test digest, disposable candidate snapshot, absent/timeout/changed/failing/mutating checks, complete tuple identity, and final recheck reject false merge-ready.

Transition tests prove positive eligibility, pre-launch repairCount≤2 with crash consumption, repeated/non-candidate stop, TERM/KILL/exit cancellation, switch refusal, proven-dead lease adoption, child reconciliation, and non-favorable termination, receipt invalidation, one terminal follow-up, zero integration invocation, and unchanged primary/ref/remote/deployment state.
Project regression gate remains scripts/verify.sh; agent-backed benchmark adoption follows after controller correctness.

blocks.title: Security boundary
blocks.text: The first implementation may be enabled only for trusted local repositories. --no-extensions and a worktree narrow capabilities but do not isolate the child process from the host. Untrusted unattended execution remains blocked until container or micro-VM routing is integrated and tested.
